title: Grateful Dead Live at Student Center, Modesto Jr College on 1969-03-28
lineage: MSC >> Nakamichi CR7a => Korg MR-1000 >> DSF [1-bit 5.6448 MHz Stereo] >> Korg MR-1000 => Korg AudioGate >> WAV [24/96]

ai_review.summary: Smooth, rich soundboard capture of a high‑energy Modesto show with a smoking School Girl opener, Dark Star → St Stephen flow and a soaring Other One.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its smooth, rich sound and excellent azimuth tuning, delivering a crystal‑clear soundboard experience. The performance bursts with energy – the band opens strong with “Good Morning Little Schoolgirl,” rolls through an unforgettable Dark Star into St Stephen and The Eleven, and caps it off with a monster Other One that many reviewers call out as a highlight. Overall both the music and the audio quality are described as exceptional.

ai_rating.rationale: All detailed reviews praise both the musical performance (standout jams, high energy) and the recording (smooth, rich, well‑tuned soundboard), yielding an almost flawless combined impression.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Smooth and rich tone with sharp guitar attack; azimuth tuning handled expertly; overall crisp mix, only a minor comment about a short drum edit that doesn’t detract from the listening experience.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set flows like the Fillmore West shows of early ’69, opening strong with School Girl and moving through a seamless Dark Star → St Stephen transition, followed by The Eleven and culminating in an expansive Other One.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar is described as edgy, sharp‑attacked, and even ‘Black Sabbath‑like’; vocals are laid back yet powerful; overall tone praised throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Pigpen’s vocal storytelling gets special mention for its lyrical swagger and leading the band through “Lovelight” (the Eleven) with great harmonies.
band_member_comments.Drums: A brief 18‑second drum segment is noted as a buzzkill edit, but no criticism of the playing itself.
